hypothesis: Ryukyu white and bluish-purple states can be polarized as loss/suppression, retention, recruitment, ancestral polymorphism, or true reactivation
primary_contrast: C. brevicaule white vs C. irumtiense bluish-purple plus Taiwan/Japan relatives
required_molecular_evidence: pigment chemistry and/or pathway state needed for mechanistic labels
current_inputs: Chang 2026 nuclear phylotranscriptomics; verified visible corolla states; PRJNA1311153 leaf RNA-seq
positive_result_would_support: a white internal state followed by coloured descendant creates a recruitment/reactivation candidate
negative_result_would_support: coloured ancestral continuity supports retention plus possible white loss/suppression
claim_ceiling: ancestral visible-colour history only until pigment evidence is added
next_gate: freeze reproducible nuclear tree/taxon mapping and run visible-state reconstruction with uncertainty

hypothesis: White Cirsium states often retain intact anthocyanin-pathway coding capacity rather than carrying irreversible structural-gene loss
required_molecular_evidence: positive detection of intact orthologous coding sequence; genomic evidence required before treating non-detection as gene loss
positive_result_would_support: intact DFR/ANS/core-pathway orthologs in white lineages falsify a simple irreversible structural-loss model
negative_result_would_support: confirmed genomic disruption/pseudogenization in white lineage supports structural loss
next_gate: targeted orthology/coding-integrity screen on expressed genes; genome follow-up for missing targets

hypothesis: White and bluish-purple C. japonicum var. takaoense morphs reflect a regulatory switch with little broad genomic divergence
required_molecular_evidence: morph-linked petal pigment/expression or securely morph-linked genomic samples
current_inputs: published morph polymorphism; leaf runs for var. takaoense; no verified run-to-colour-morph mapping
positive_result_would_support: shared genomic background with morph-linked petal regulatory differences would strongly support switch/recruitment
negative_result_would_support: deep genomic structuring by colour morph would weaken a simple regulatory-switch model
next_gate: recover supplementary/voucher evidence linking sequenced individuals to W/BP morphs or collect new morph-linked petal material

hypothesis: Broad Camellia colour history contains repeated white/red/yellow transitions and a likely white ancestral state
required_molecular_evidence: visible-colour states sufficient for phenotype reconstruction; chemistry needed for mechanistic transitions
positive_result_would_support: independent reconstruction matching white MRCA and repeated transitions would reproduce phenotype history
negative_result_would_support: different open nuclear topology/state coding could overturn published polarization
next_gate: obtain request-only raw/tree inputs or build an independent sufficiently broad open nuclear tree

hypothesis: Southeast Asian/southern China yellow lineages are not one taxonomically independent origin and may include retention, repeated recruitment, or hybrid transfer
primary_contrast: public 20 golden Camellia leaf transcriptomes plus Vietnam anchor
required_molecular_evidence: yellow pigment chemistry cannot be assumed identical across taxa
current_inputs: PRJNA1050624 / 20 SRRs; 2025 species-concept audit; 2026 yellow paper as published-only evidence
positive_result_would_support: multiple independent nuclear lineages with distinct coding/regulatory architecture support repeated/heterogeneous deployment
negative_result_would_support: collapse of nominal species into complexes plus reticulation reduces apparent number of independent yellow events
claim_ceiling: yellow-lineage coding/history comparison; not genus-wide origin count
next_gate: reconstruct/open nuclear backbone after taxonomic reconciliation; add non-yellow outgroups before counting yellow gains

hypothesis: Golden-yellow phenotype can combine independent flavonol and carotenoid deployment rather than represent a single flavonol state
required_molecular_evidence: public flower RNA-seq plus metabolite evidence
current_inputs: SRP112181 15 admitted flower runs; pigment chemistry from Zhou 2017; public T2T genome
positive_result_would_support: developmentally coordinated flavonol/carotenoid pathway scores reproducing pigment accumulation supports multi-axis state
negative_result_would_support: one pathway alone explaining all molecular/pigment changes would simplify the state model
claim_ceiling: mechanistic developmental deployment in C. nitidissima
next_gate: anchor pathway loci to T2T annotation then quantify S1-S5 expression

hypothesis: Different yellow lineages may deploy distinct molecular routes despite the same visible phenotype
primary_contrast: C. nitidissima vs public golden-20 lineages including C. insularis and C. longruiensis/flavida complex
required_molecular_evidence: cross-lineage coding architecture plus taxon-specific pigment chemistry/expression where available
current_inputs: public golden-20 leaf transcriptomes; C. nitidissima flower data/T2T; published WRKY23-FLS in longruiensis
positive_result_would_support: different FLS/regulator/carotenoid architectures support mechanistic heterogeneity/convergence at phenotype level

claim_ceiling: coding-architecture comparison only until chemistry expands
next_gate: complete FLS/core-pathway orthology across public yellow transcriptomes; prioritize chemical evidence for distinct Vietnam trajectory

hypothesis: Repeated flower-colour evolution often uses regulatory/tissue-specific redeployment of conserved pigment machinery rather than repeated de novo invention
primary_contrast: independent colour transitions in both families
required_molecular_evidence: coding retention through suppressed states plus tissue-specific activation/regulation at later coloured states
current_inputs: Cirsium public leaf data; Camellia public flower/T2T data; published functional Camellia mechanisms
positive_result_would_support: parallel retention + regulatory redeployment in independent transitions supports network-level convergence
negative_result_would_support: recurrent structural-gene destruction/de novo replacement or no evidence of latent pathway retention weakens the model
claim_ceiling: comparative mechanism only after at least one strong transition per family passes E3 evidence
next_gate: obtain a molecularly resolved reactivation/recruitment transition in Cirsium; finish open Camellia mechanism/history integration
